name: East Turkestan Republic (Second East Turkestan Republic)

predecessors.name: Republic of China
predecessors.text: the Ili, Tarbagatay and Altay districts of Xinjiang Province (infobox predecessor: Xinjiang Province, Republic of China)

successors.name: People's Republic of China
successors.text: the Three Districts, whose National Army was 'incorporated into the People's Liberation Army as the Xinjiang 5th Army Corps' on 20 December 1949

ledger.x: 12 November 1944: the East Turkestan Republic is proclaimed at Ghulja.
October-November 1944: the rising spreads to the Tarbagatay and Altay districts.
September 1945: the Ili National Army reaches the Manas River.
2 January 1946: a preliminary peace is signed at Dihua.
27 June 1946: the republic becomes the Ili District Council.
20 December 1949: the Three Districts' National Army joins the People's Liberation Army.

wars.name: Ili Rebellion (Three Districts Revolution)
wars.outcome: Ghulja stormed 7-13 November 1944; the Ili forces took the oil fields at Dushanzi in September 1945 and stood on the Manasi River; Soviet-mediated talks opened on 14 October 1945, a preliminary peace was signed on 2 January 1946 and the agreement of June 1946…

wars.name: Osman Batur's offensive in the Ashan zone
wars.outcome: In September 1947, in a Chinese-supported offensive, Osman Batur's Kazakhs 'defeated and killed ETR forces in the Ashan zone and seized most of its towns'; the pages do not say how the zone was held afterwards.

certainty.note: No boundary line is described on either page; the Three Districts are administrative units and the Manasi River front of September 1945 was a battle line.
